title: 7 November Sepoy-Janata Uprising
subtitle: Soldier unrest, factional politics, and competing memories reshape the post-August 1975 crisis.
summary: On 7 November 1975, amid coups and counter-coups after the August and jail killings, sections of soldiers and political activists mobilized in Dhaka. The upheaval helped bring Ziaur Rahman to the center of state power, while its meaning remains sharply contested in Bangladesh's political memory.
heroTagline: A post-August crisis turned barracks politics into a new national power struggle.
whyItMatters: The November upheaval links the 1975 assassinations to later military-backed rule, party formation, and rival commemoration traditions, making it central to understanding post-liberation state instability.

historicalDebate: Political traditions describe 7 November in sharply different ways, including as a soldier-people uprising, a coup sequence, or a moment of violent factional reordering. This page treats the chronology separately from later partisan memory.
